title: Clean Stock & Tissue-Culture Fundamentals
level: Propagation & Clean Stock Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners progressing through the Propagation & Clean Stock Specialist pathway
Propagation personnel responsible for clean-stock, tissue-culture, production-planning or propagation-quality workflows
prerequisites: COURSE-LH-PCS-001 through COURSE-LH-PCS-004 or approved equivalents
Approved tissue-culture laboratory safety and site-specific aseptic-work training where practical work is performed
evidencePolicy: Cannabis-specific micropropagation and regeneration studies support genotype-dependent establishment, multiplication, rooting, acclimation and fidelity concerns. Plant-pathology evidence supports testing-aware clean-stock controls. Exact media, plant-growth regulators, disinfection methods, test panels and release criteria remain controlled by validated laboratory procedures, product labels, qualified technical authority and applicable law.
assessmentPolicy: The specialist assessment remains development-only until technical, assessment and accessibility review plus pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize independent laboratory operation, pathogen-free claims, diagnostic release, chemical selection or disposition of controlled material.
description: Develops specialist clean-stock reasoning from source identity and aseptic establishment through multiplication, rooting, acclimation, fidelity monitoring and evidence-based material release.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish identity, observed health, test status and release status when building a clean-stock record and material-status decision.
Design and execute a traceable aseptic workflow that separates clean and exposed states, detects breaches and preserves batch identity.
Interpret establishment and contamination patterns by source, explant, vessel, timing and process history, then select an evidence-preserving response.
Compare multiplication or regeneration treatments using genotype-aware quality measures rather than shoot count alone.
Evaluate in-vitro material through rooting, ex-vitro acclimation, fidelity monitoring and controlled release using stage-specific evidence.
